submitter: travelling-docs thread (tooldoctraveller4), 2026-07-20 — ROUND 5, RESHAPED after owner ruling
rationale:
ROUND 5 of submission 7ef4de4e. This is NOT a revision of round 4's plan — it REPLACES two of its three edits, on the owner's ruling, and the council should judge it fresh.

WHAT THE OWNER RULED. Round 4 ended 8 approve / 2 object. improvement_guardian's open objection (MEDIUM, and correct) was that edit 1 leaned on createRerenderWorkItem, whose raw-SQL INSERT bypasses insertWorkItem's dedup/two-strike machinery — and my own rationale had TOUTED that bypass, because it dodged the two-strike bug. Reusing a contract-violating shape to fix a bug entrenches it. The owner's words: 'don't write the bypass, fix the two strike rule.' That has been done and committed (f6e3f3166, workItem.recurrenceExpected, 6 tests, opt-in and therefore INERT until a caller sets it).

WHAT THAT RULING EXPOSED, and why this plan is smaller. Round 4's edit 1 moved the re-render REQUEST out of tool-improver's workflow config and into update_component_html_action.go, and edit 3 (migration 171) deleted the now-redundant workflow step. Both of those exist only because I believed the config-driven step could not be made correct. It can. tool-improver's create_rerender_item step uses the create_work_item action, and create_work_item ALREADY calls insertWorkItem (create_work_item_action.go:170) — it is the normal path, not a bypass. So the correct fix is not to move the request into Go; it is to make the existing request carry what the pipeline needs. No step is deleted, no dangling complete.config.output_fields reference is created (the defect the reviewers' own read-only check found in round 1), and nothing moves between layers.

WHY THE ITEM IS BORN DEAD, precisely, in the order the values are consumed. (1) create_work_item builds item_key as '<prefix>_<domain>' (create_work_item_action.go:128) — SITE-wide. tool-improver's prefix is rerender_tool_fix, so every tool on a site shares one key. (2) insertWorkItem's anti-churn block counts prior terminal items on that key; for an ACTION REQUEST a 'complete' predecessor is a SUCCESS, not a strike, so after two successful re-renders the third is born 'unresolved' and never dispatched. LIVE PROOF on the benchmark page, item history: two needs_rerender 'complete' (2026-07-17 15:11, 20:00), then '[unresolved after 2 attempts] Re-render page after tool improvement' on 07-18 10:02 AND 07-19 10:40. (3) Even when an item does dispatch, its spec carries no reason, so page-rerender's check_rerender_mode falls to else_step render_page = rerender_single_page = 'Simple concatenation - no template re-rendering', which ships the stale stored HTML and reports success. (4) And forcing the correct branch escalates instead of rendering, because the content pre-check refuses any section with empty content_data — which a tool has BY DESIGN.

THE PROPAGATION IS ALREADY WIRED — this is the load-bearing new fact, verified live this session, and it is why edit 4 is config and not code. rerender-pages' create_rerender_items step config maps reason -> input_data.spec.reason and component_id -> input_data.spec.component_id. create_rerender_items_action.go:139 sets scoped = (reason == 'section_data_resolved' || reason == 'image_landed') && componentIDStr != '', and line 243-244 stamps that reason onto each per-page page_rerender item, which is exactly what check_rerender_mode gates on. So if tool-improver's needs_rerender item carries BOTH reason and component_id in its spec, the whole chain already works. It carries neither. The only reason it cannot is that create_work_item's spec_data is a PATH into collected data, never a literal (ExtractActionInputs Strategy 0 resolves config[field] only when it is a dot-containing string — action_inputs.go:126-131), so no workflow step can stamp a constant like reason.

WHAT I AM ASKING FOR. Two additive, default-off affordances on create_work_item (spec composition; key scoping + recurrence opt-in), one guard exemption keyed on an EXPLICIT marker, and one config migration. Every existing caller of create_work_item is byte-identical in behaviour unless it opts in.

ONE THING I GOT WRONG THIS SESSION, on the record. I read the benchmark page's build_status='needs_rebuild' as a fifth blocker, on the assumption that get_pages_for_rerender would exclude it. It does not: queryPagesMetadata filters on p.status (get_pages_for_rerender_action.go:153, 'AND p.status IN (...)'), and the page's status is 'active'. Not a blocker. I record it because the same misread would have added a spurious edit.

SEQUENCING, which is better than round 4's. Round 4 had a genuine hazard: migration 171 DELETED the only re-render request, so applying it before the image shipped would leave none at all, and it needed a pod-grep pre-flight to guard. This plan has no such hazard in either order — the migration only ADDS config keys, which an old binary ignores as unknown config, and the new binary ignores absent keys. The two halves are independently inert and compose when both are live.

plan.summary: A tool-improver fix is written to content_components.html_template and never rendered onto the page, so every re-verification tests an unchanged page (bugs_open/024; the benchmark's rendered_html is still 9,901 chars = its v1 born length while the template is 10,626 and carries the fix). The re-render request exists but is born dead: its item_key is site-wide, so insertWorkItem's two-strike rule brands it 'unresolved' after two SUCCESSFUL predecessors; and its spec carries no reason/component_id, so create_rerender_items never stamps the section-rerender reason and page-rerender assembles stale HTML instead. Fix: give create_work_item the ability to compose a spec from literals and paths, to scope its item_key, and to opt into the already-committed recurrenceExpected flag; exempt genuine tool sections (explicit marker component_level='tool' + empty input_schema) from the empty-content_data escalation guard; and rewire tool-improver's existing step by config to use all three. No step is deleted and no raw-SQL insert path is reused.

edits.rationale: spec_data is resolved as a PATH only, so no workflow step can stamp a constant into the item spec. That is the sole reason tool-improver cannot set reason='section_data_resolved', which is the value create_rerender_items gates on. Two explicit config keys rather than one clever one: spec_literal is verbatim, spec_paths is resolved. An unresolved spec_paths entry is a HARD ERROR, not a logged warning — this directly answers the round-4 low objection that 'both helpers only logger.Warn on failure, so a failed rerender request reverts silently to this exact bug'. A missing component_id would make create_rerender_items' scoped=false and silently degrade to assemble-only, i.e. reproduce bugs_open/024 with no signal at all. Failing loudly is the whole point.

Two independent defects at one call site. (a) item_key is '<prefix>_<domain>' — site-wide — so even with the two-strike rule fixed, two tools fixed close together collide on idx_swi_dedup (site_id, item_key) and one re-render request is simply lost. item_key_suffix_field is additive: absent or unresolved, the key is byte-identical to today, so none of the existing callers change. (b) recurrence_expected surfaces the already-committed, currently-inert workItem.recurrenceExpected as config. Default false. This is the flag the owner asked for instead of the bypass, and this edit is the caller that makes f6e3f3166 do anything at all.

UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE from round 4's edit 2, which carried 8 approvals including bug_historian's after it was re-keyed onto the explicit marker. The pre-check escalates any section with empty content_data; check_escalated then routes true -> complete, bypassing save_sections, the ONLY writer of rendered_html — so the render is computed and thrown away. That guard is right for its original purpose (the blanked article bodies, bugs_closed/004 and 005) but has no concept of a section type that has no content_data BY DESIGN. Keyed on the explicit component_level='tool' marker AND an empty input_schema, both already present on comp — component_level is SELECTed by loadSectionComponents (v3_site_actions.go:3396, COALESCE(component_level,'section')) and carried on componentInfo.Raw, so there is no new query and no struct change. Not keyed on a heuristic: bug_historian's round-1 objection was that predicating on 'no required LLM fields' exempted a broader class than justified, including components with OPTIONAL source:'llm' fields. The marker is exact — 12 of 122 active components.

Makes tool-improver's EXISTING step use the three affordances above. This replaces round 4's migration 171, which deleted the step; nothing is deleted here, so complete.config.output_fields' reference to 'rerender_item' stays valid — the dangling-reference defect the reviewers' own read-only check found in round 1 cannot arise. spec_paths uses update_result.component_id (not tool_data.component_id) so the spec is tied to the write that actually succeeded; update_component has error_step refuse_mangled_write, so a failed write never reaches this step. Number is 179, not 178: ledger max is 176, but 177_council_tolerate_truncation.sql and 178_news_listing_js_progressive_enhancement.sql exist on disk with no ledger rows (the bugs_open/007 trap, re-armed — reported, not silently worked around). Needle-gated on the pre-state so a re-run is a 0-row no-op; RETURNING asserts the post-condition inline; snapshot first.
edits.sketch:
BEGIN;

SELECT snapshot_agent('tool-improver', 'bugs_open/024: stamp reason+component_id, scope the item_key, opt into recurrence');

-- Needle gate: only act on the pre-state. A re-run matches nothing and is a
-- 0-row no-op rather than a second, differently-shaped write.
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(
      default_config,
      '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}',
      (default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}')
        || jsonb_build_object(
             'recurrence_expected', true,
             'spec_literal', jsonb_build_object('reason', 'section_data_resolved'),
             'spec_paths',   jsonb_build_object('component_id', 'update_result.component_id'),
             'item_key_suffix_field', 'update_result.component_id'
           )
    ),
    updated_at = NOW()
WHERE type = 'tool-improver'
  AND is_active = true
  AND default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}' IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT (default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}' ? 'spec_literal')
RETURNING type,
          default_config #>> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config,spec_literal,reason}' AS reason,
          default_config #>> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config,spec_paths,component_id}' AS component_path,
          (default_config #> '{workflow,steps,create_rerender_item,config}' ? 'recurrence_expected') AS has_recurrence;

INSERT INTO schema_migrations (filename) VALUES ('179_tool_improver_rerender_request.sql');

COMMIT;

plan.risks:
1) THE BIGGEST RISK IS THE ONE I AM ASKING FOR: spec_paths turns a previously-silent condition into a hard failure. If a step configures spec_paths and the path does not resolve, the orchestration now errors instead of creating a spec-less item. That is deliberate — a silently incomplete spec is precisely how bugs_open/024 hid for three cycles — but it means a mis-typed path in a future migration fails the run rather than degrading. Only tool-improver opts in, so today the blast radius is one step. Reviewers should confirm they agree the loud failure is the right trade, and that update_result.component_id genuinely resolves (update_component_html_action.go's return map includes "component_id": componentIDStr, and its step's output_field is update_result).

2) Edit 3 changes shared re-render machinery used by every site. Mitigation: the predicate is the explicit marker AND an empty input_schema, and it only SKIPS a pre-check — it never writes. The population is 12 of 122 active components. A component mis-labelled component_level='tool' that genuinely needs content_data would render an empty section; the marker is set at component creation and is not user-editable, and no tool has an input_schema.

3) THE DISCLOSED RESIDUAL FROM ROUND 4 STANDS AND IS STILL NOT FIXED HERE: plan_sections_action.go:1090-1108 defers (and therefore CARRIES rather than re-renders) an empty-schema component when comp.Function contains 'article', 'content', 'body', 'text' or 'blog'. tool-loot-table-balancer matches none, so it returns 'ready'. A future 'tool-content-planner' would be silently carried — the same silent-carry-by-heuristic shape as the bug being fixed, one function away. Named again so it does not arrive as a surprise later.

4) The item_key suffix changes the dedup identity for the opted-in step, so an OPEN item under the old site-wide key will not dedup against a new component-scoped one; a single duplicate re-render is possible across the migration boundary. A re-render is idempotent, so the cost is one wasted run, not damage.

5) recurrence_expected waives the anti-churn heuristics for this step, so a genuinely broken tool could re-request a re-render every cycle instead of being labelled unresolved after two. That is the intended trade (the label was firing on SUCCESS), but it does remove a churn signal — the compensating signal is the Tier-4 acceptance verdict, which stays red and is the thing bugs_open/010's convergence guard is meant to catch. Dedup is NOT waived, so concurrent duplicates are still refused.

6) NOT VERIFIED END-TO-END YET, and cannot be until an image ships: the Go here is inert until the chassis rolls past v1.0.1139. The proof is the benchmark going green on mobile-fit@mobile, and I will not hand-fix it to get there. What reviewers can check now is the propagation chain, which is live config and quoted verbatim above.
